column3: The Hebrew introduces the report with a passive, “it was heard”; BSB makes the enemies active hearers.
The Hebrew calls the letter open; BSB calls it unsealed.
The Hebrew says Geshem “says”; BSB says he agrees.
The Hebrew says “now” and that these words will be heard by the king; BSB says “Soon” and supplies reaching the king’s ears.
The Hebrew says the reported events did not happen and pictures invention as coming from his heart; BSB says there is nothing to the rumors and locates invention in his mind.
The Hebrew does not explicitly address “my God” at the end, as BSB does. It says the work will not be done; BSB says it will never be finished.
The Hebrew says he was confined without explicitly repeating “to his house,” which BSB supplies.
The Hebrew asks who like him could enter the temple and live; BSB describes entering to save his own life.
The Hebrew separately lists fearing, doing so, and sinning; BSB makes sinning the result of doing as suggested.
The Hebrew says “according to these deeds of his,” using a singular possessor; BSB says “for what they have done.”
The Hebrew says the surrounding nations saw and fell greatly in their own eyes; BSB says they were afraid and disheartened.
The Hebrew leaves the plural reporters unnamed and refers to “his good deeds”; BSB identifies them as the nobles and names Tobiah.
